name: Citizen Agent Sim
description: Runs a population of needs-driven agents that commute between home, work, and commerce on a daily schedule, making the abstract zone grid legible as a living city. Each citizen holds a home assignment, a job assignment, and a satisfaction value derived from commute length and unmet needs; a citizen whose needs stay unmet long enough leaves, which is the feedback loop that punishes bad planning without a fail state. Pathing between destinations is delegated to movement.pathfinding_system — this component decides where a citizen wants to go and why, never how to walk there. It does not own the needs meters themselves (social.needs_decay owns per-agent meter decay for the life-sim scale) nor the zone supply it consumes (world.zone_planner owns that); it is the assignment and itinerary layer that sits between the two, and it is intentionally reusable by any genre that needs believable background population rather than individually simulated protagonists.

inputs.name: populationCap
inputs.description: Hard ceiling on simultaneously simulated agents. Beyond this, new arrivals are counted statistically rather than simulated, which keeps tick cost flat as the city grows.

inputs.name: commuteToleranceMinutes
inputs.description: In-game minutes of commute a citizen accepts before satisfaction decays. The single strongest lever for 'traffic matters' versus 'traffic is flavor'.

inputs.name: unhappyDepartureDays
inputs.description: In-game days of sustained unhappiness before a citizen abandons their home and job. Long enough that one bad week is recoverable, short enough that neglect hollows out a district.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: Daily itinerary anchors in world.day_night_cycle hours. All citizens share the anchors with per-agent jitter, so rush hours emerge instead of being scripted.

outputs.name: population
outputs.description: Current simulated citizen count, distinct from any statistical overflow beyond populationCap.

outputs.name: averageSatisfaction
outputs.description: Population-wide satisfaction in [0, 1], the headline number demand indicators and win conditions should read rather than sampling agents individually.

outputs.name: commuteLoad
outputs.description: Per-route agent counts for the current commute window, so road or transit visualization can be driven by real itineraries.
